title: The CDC suggests a toy where a button press makes something happen
summary: The CDC's two-year tips suggest toys where the child pushes a button and something happens, to learn how things work.
body: In the activities for a two-year-old, the CDC says to give toys that teach how to make things work and how to solve problems. Its example is a toy where the child pushes a button and something happens. That is a suggested activity. It is not the milestone line about switches and knobs. The suggestion comes from the US page, and it is not a required purchase. The activity is a toy whose control, once pressed, makes an outcome the child can see.

sources.title: Milestones by 2 Years
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US CDC page, public domain. Updated and reviewed 16 May 2026. Supports the activity sentence about toys where the child pushes a button and something happens.
